#         # api-contract-dual-hyper-reqwest-001

        **Suite:** dependency_management | **Type:** api_contract | **Difficulty:** hard
        **Repos:** hyper + reqwest

        ## Context

        Between the versions pinned in this workspace, hyper made a breaking
change to how it represents request/response bodies, and reqwest is pinned
to a version that predates that change. The reqwest HTTP client depends
heavily on hyper's body-related types in its client implementation.

Your task:
1. Find where hyper defines its body-related types and traits in this
   version, and work out what changed relative to what reqwest expects.
2. Find where reqwest uses hyper's body type(s) in its client implementation.
3. Identify the contract mismatch between hyper's current body types
   and reqwest's existing usage.
4. Document the migration path for each affected reqwest module, citing the
   specific files, types, and functions involved on both sides.

Write your analysis to /workspace/analysis/IMPACT_REPORT.md

        ## Expected Output

        Write your analysis to `/workspace/analysis/IMPACT_REPORT.md`.

        Your report should include:
        - File paths from each repository that are relevant
        - Specific code symbols, functions, or types involved
        - The nature of each change (removal, rename, signature change, behavioral)
        - Migration recommendations

        ## Hints

        - All repos are cloned under `/workspace/`
        - Focus on import/dependency declarations first, then trace into implementation
        - Check version constraints in dependency manifests (Cargo.toml, go.mod, pom.xml, requirements.txt)

# IMPACT_REPORT.md — hyper v1.0.0 vs. reqwest v0.11.22: Body API Contract Analysis

> **Repos analysed:**
> - [`github.com/sg-evals/hyper--v1.0.0`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/hyper--v1.0.0) — hyper v1.0.0
> - [`github.com/sg-evals/reqwest--v0.11.22`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/reqwest--v0.11.22) — reqwest v0.11.22

---

## 1. Dependency Version Mismatch

**reqwest** [`Cargo.toml` line 103](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/reqwest--v0.11.22/-/blob/Cargo.toml?L103-L104):
```toml
hyper     = { version = "0.14.21", features = ["tcp","http1","http2","client","runtime"] }
http-body = "0.4.0"
http      = "0.2"
```

**hyper v1.0.0** [`Cargo.toml` lines 26–28](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/hyper--v1.0.0/-/blob/Cargo.toml?L26-L28):
```toml
http      = "1"
http-body = "1"
```

The two crates sit on incompatible major versions of three shared crates. This is not resolvable with feature flags — a source-level migration is required for all five affected reqwest modules.

---

## 2. Body Type Architecture: What Changed

### hyper v0.14 (what reqwest expects)

| Symbol | Kind |
|--------|------|
| `hyper::Body` | **concrete struct** — unified send/receive body |
| `hyper::body::Sender` | public struct from `hyper::Body::channel()` |
| `hyper::body::HttpBody` | re-export of the `http-body 0.4` trait |
| `http_body::Body` (0.4) | trait with `poll_data` + `poll_trailers` methods |
| `hyper::body::to_bytes()` | collects body into `Bytes` |
| `hyper::Client<C, B>` | high-level pooling HTTP client |

### hyper v1.0.0 (current — [`src/body/mod.rs`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/hyper--v1.0.0/-/blob/src/body/mod.rs))

| Symbol | Kind |
|--------|------|
| `hyper::body::Incoming` | concrete struct — **receive-only** (server req / client response) |
| `hyper::body::Body` | **trait re-export** from `http-body 1.x` — no longer a concrete type |
| `hyper::body::Frame<D>` | new unified data+trailers frame type |
| `hyper::body::SizeHint` | re-export from `http-body 1.x` |
| `hyper::Client` | **REMOVED** — moved to `hyper-util` crate |
| `hyper::body::to_bytes()` | **REMOVED** — moved to `http-body-util` crate |
| `hyper::body::HttpBody` | **REMOVED** — replaced by `http_body::Body` (1.x) |

---

## 3. The Core Breaking Change: `http-body` 0.4 → 1.x Trait

reqwest implements `http_body::Body` (0.4) in three places. The old two-method model:

```rust
// http-body 0.4 (reqwest's current model)
fn poll_data(self: Pin<&mut Self>, cx: &mut Context) -> Poll<Option<Result<Data, E>>>;
fn poll_trailers(self: Pin<&mut Self>, cx: &mut Context) -> Poll<Result<Option<HeaderMap>, E>>;
```

hyper v1.0.0 re-exports `http-body 1.x`, which **removes both methods** in favour of:

```rust
// http-body 1.x (hyper v1 model — Incoming::poll_frame in src/body/incoming.rs L174)
fn poll_frame(self: Pin<&mut Self>, cx: &mut Context) -> Poll<Option<Result<Frame<Data>, E>>>;
```

`Frame<D>` (used in [`src/body/incoming.rs` lines 190–201](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/hyper--v1.0.0/-/blob/src/body/incoming.rs?L190-L201)) carries either data bytes (`Frame::data(chunk)`) or trailers (`Frame::trailers(header_map)`).

---

## 4. Affected reqwest Files

---

### 4.1 [`src/async_impl/body.rs`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/reqwest--v0.11.22/-/blob/src/async_impl/body.rs)

| Location | Symbol | Issue | Type |
|----------|--------|-------|------|
| [line 45](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/reqwest--v0.11.22/-/blob/src/async_impl/body.rs?L45) | `struct WrapHyper(hyper::Body)` | `hyper::Body` removed | Removal |
| [lines 330–358](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/reqwest--v0.11.22/-/blob/src/async_impl/body.rs?L330-L358) | `impl HttpBody for WrapHyper` — `poll_data`, `poll_trailers` | Methods removed from trait | Trait method change |
| [line 111](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/reqwest--v0.11.22/-/blob/src/async_impl/body.rs?L111) | `Body::response(body: hyper::Body, ...)` | `hyper::Body` removed | Signature change |
| [line 121](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/reqwest--v0.11.22/-/blob/src/async_impl/body.rs?L121) | `Body::wrap(body: hyper::Body)` | `hyper::Body` removed | Signature change |
| [lines 169–179](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/reqwest--v0.11.22/-/blob/src/async_impl/body.rs?L169-L179) | `impl From<hyper::Body> for Body` | `hyper::Body` removed | Removal |
| [lines 233–290](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/reqwest--v0.11.22/-/blob/src/async_impl/body.rs?L233-L290) | `impl HttpBody for ImplStream` — `poll_data`, `poll_trailers` | Methods removed from trait | Trait method change |
| [lines 302–326](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/reqwest--v0.11.22/-/blob/src/async_impl/body.rs?L302-L326) | `impl HttpBody for WrapStream` — `poll_data`, `poll_trailers` | Methods removed from trait | Trait method change |

**Migration:**
- `struct WrapHyper(hyper::Body)` → `struct WrapHyper(hyper::body::Incoming)`
- All `impl HttpBody` blocks: replace `poll_data` + `poll_trailers` with `poll_frame`. Since none produce trailers, wrap data as `Frame::data(chunk)`.
- `Body::response` / `Body::wrap`: accept `hyper::body::Incoming` instead of `hyper::Body`.
- Replace `From<hyper::Body>` with `From<hyper::body::Incoming>`.

---

### 4.2 [`src/async_impl/decoder.rs`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/reqwest--v0.11.22/-/blob/src/async_impl/decoder.rs)

| Location | Symbol | Issue | Type |
|----------|--------|-------|------|
| [line 19](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/reqwest--v0.11.22/-/blob/src/async_impl/decoder.rs?L19) | `use hyper::body::HttpBody` | `HttpBody` re-export removed in hyper v1 | Removal |
| [lines 264–269](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/reqwest--v0.11.22/-/blob/src/async_impl/decoder.rs?L264-L269) | `fn poll_data(...)` | Method removed from trait | Trait method change |
| [lines 271–276](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/reqwest--v0.11.22/-/blob/src/async_impl/decoder.rs?L271-L276) | `fn poll_trailers(...)` | Method removed from trait | Trait method change |
| [lines 278–285](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/reqwest--v0.11.22/-/blob/src/async_impl/decoder.rs?L278-L285) | `HttpBody::size_hint(body)` UFCS | Import path changes | API change |

**Migration:**
- Replace `use hyper::body::HttpBody` with `use http_body::Body as HttpBody`.
- Rewrite `impl HttpBody for Decoder` with a single `poll_frame` that wraps `self.poll_next(cx)` output as `Frame::data(chunk)`. Decoder never produces trailers.

### 4.3 [`src/async_impl/response.rs`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/reqwest--v0.11.22/-/blob/src/async_impl/response.rs)

| [line 34](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/reqwest--v0.11.22/-/blob/src/async_impl/response.rs?L34) | `fn new(res: hyper::Response<hyper::Body>, ...)` | `hyper::Body` removed | Signature change |
| [lines 81–84](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/reqwest--v0.11.22/-/blob/src/async_impl/response.rs?L81-L84) | `use hyper::body::HttpBody; HttpBody::size_hint(...)` | `hyper::body::HttpBody` removed | Removal |

**Migration:**
- `fn new` signature: `hyper::Response<hyper::Body>` → `hyper::Response<hyper::body::Incoming>`.
- Add `http-body-util = "0.1"` dependency. Replace `hyper::body::to_bytes(...)` with:
  ```rust
  use http_body_util::BodyExt;
  self.res.into_body().collect().await?.to_bytes()
  ```
- Replace `use hyper::body::HttpBody` with `use http_body::Body as HttpBody`.
- Replace `hyper::client::connect::HttpInfo` with `hyper_util::client::legacy::connect::HttpInfo`.

| Location | Symbol | Issue | Type |

| [line 16](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/reqwest--v0.11.22/-/blob/src/async_impl/client.rs?L16) | `use hyper::client::{HttpConnector, ResponseFuture as HyperResponseFuture}` | Both moved to `hyper-util` | Removal |
| [line 615](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/reqwest--v0.11.22/-/blob/src/async_impl/client.rs?L615) | `hyper::Client::builder()` | `hyper::Client` removed from hyper v1 | Removal |
| [line 684](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/reqwest--v0.11.22/-/blob/src/async_impl/client.rs?L684) | `builder.build(connector)` | Client builder API changed | Behavioral |
| [line 1648](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/reqwest--v0.11.22/-/blob/src/async_impl/client.rs?L1648) | `type HyperClient = hyper::Client<Connector, super::body::ImplStream>` | `hyper::Client<C, B>` removed | Removal |

The hyper v1 [`src/client/mod.rs`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/hyper--v1.0.0/-/blob/src/client/mod.rs) only exposes `client::conn` (low-level per-connection management). There is no pooling `Client` anymore.

**Migration:**
- Add `hyper-util = { version = "0.1", features = ["client", "client-legacy", "http1", "http2"] }` to Cargo.toml.
- Replace `hyper::Client` → `hyper_util::client::legacy::Client`.
- Replace `hyper::client::HttpConnector` → `hyper_util::client::legacy::connect::HttpConnector`.
- Replace `hyper::client::ResponseFuture` → `hyper_util::client::legacy::ResponseFuture`.
- Verify HTTP/2 builder methods (e.g. `http2_initial_stream_window_size`, `http2_adaptive_window`, `http09_responses`, `http1_title_case_headers`) against hyper-util 0.1 API — several were reorganised.
- `ImplStream` must implement `http-body 1.x Body` (see §4.1).

**Migration:**
- Replace `hyper::Body::channel()` with `futures_channel::mpsc::channel::<Result<Bytes, crate::Error>>(0)`.

- OR use `http_body_util::StreamBody<futures_channel::mpsc::Receiver<...>>` as the body.
- Replace the `Sender.tx: hyper::body::Sender` field with `futures_channel::mpsc::Sender<Result<Bytes, crate::Error>>` and adapt the `send_data` call accordingly.

## 6. New / Updated Dependencies

**Add:**
```toml
http-body-util = "0.1"   # BodyExt::collect(), StreamBody (replaces hyper::body::to_bytes + channel bodies)
hyper-util = { version = "0.1", features = ["client", "client-legacy", "http1", "http2"] }
```

**Update:**
| Crate | From | To |
|-------|------|----|
| `hyper` | `"0.14.21"` | `"1.0"` |
| `http-body` | `"0.4.0"` | `"1"` |
| `http` | `"0.2"` | `"1"` |
| `h2` | `"0.3.10"` | `"0.4"` |
| `hyper-tls` | `"0.5"` | hyper-1-compatible version |
| `hyper-rustls` | `"0.24.0"` | `"0.27"` (hyper 1 compatible) |

---

## 7. Behavioural Notes

- **Trailers:** All current reqwest `poll_trailers` implementations return `Poll::Ready(Ok(None))` — trailers are never produced. When migrating to `poll_frame`, these bodies can safely emit only `Frame::data(chunk)` frames and return `Poll::Ready(None)` when the stream ends. No trailer-handling logic needs to be ported.

- **`hyper::Client` removal** is the largest single impact. reqwest currently delegates connection pooling entirely to `hyper::Client`'s internal pool. The `hyper_util::client::legacy::Client` provides a compatible (but not identical) API; all builder-method calls must be audited against the hyper-util 0.1 documentation.

- **`http` crate major version:** `http` v0.2 and v1 are type-incompatible at the Rust type-system level. `http::HeaderMap`, `http::Request`, `http::Response`, `http::StatusCode`, `http::Uri`, `http::Method` are all distinct types across the two versions. Since reqwest exposes these in its public API, upgrading `http` is itself a semver-breaking change for reqwest's downstream users.
